working: 1 + sin^4 x >= 1 while cos^2 3x <= 1, so equality forces both sides to equal 1: sin x = 0 and cos^2 3x = 1. sin x = 0 gives x = k*pi, at which 3x = 3k*pi and cos^2 3x = 1 automatically, so every such x works. In [-5pi/2, 5pi/2] = [-7.854, 7.854] the multiples of pi are k = -2,-1,0,1,2, i.e. 5 solutions. A 400k-point scan of cos^2(3x) - 1 - sin^4 x over the interval returns exactly those five points.

working: tan x + cot x = 2 gives (sin^2 x + cos^2 x)/(sin x cos x) = 2, so sin x cos x = 1/2 and sin 2x = 1, x = pi/4 + k*pi, where sin^2 x = cos^2 x = 1/2. Hence sin^{2n}x + cos^{2n}x = 2*(1/2)^n = 2^{1-n}: 1 at n=1, 1/2 at n=2, 1/4 at n=3. That is not constant, and it equals 2^n only at n=1/2 and 1/2 only at n=2, so no listed closed form is correct in general.

working: Group as 7tan^6 x (tan^2 x + 1) - 3tan^2 x (tan^2 x + 1) = sec^2 x (7 tan^6 x - 3 tan^2 x). Substituting t = tan x, dt = sec^2 x dx, with t running 0 to 1: I = int_0^1 (7t^6 - 3t^2) dt = [t^7 - t^3] from 0 to 1 = 1 - 1 = 0. So 7I = 0. Numerical quadrature of the original integrand returns I = -9e-43, i.e. zero.
